title: 3D #1 remade: r = (cos θ, sin θ, 1), θ keeps turning, angle with z? (predict-first, Remotion 3D, calm, 22 s)

captions.instagram:
NDA Maths · 3D Vectors
r = (cos θ) î + (sin θ) ĵ + k̂, and θ keeps turning. Its angle with the z-axis… A varies · B 45° · C 90°
Comment your guess before you watch 👇

r always goes up 1 and across 1 (cos²θ + sin²θ = 1). So every r is the long side of the same right triangle: |r| = √2, cos γ = 1/√2, γ = 45° for every θ → B.
As θ turns, r sweeps a cone around the z-axis.
Trap: 90° is the angle of its shadow on the floor, not of r.

NDA 2026 (II) asked exactly this (Maths Q68): angle with the +z-axis = ? Answer (c) π/4. Trap (b) π/3 comes from cos γ = 1/2: the √ in |r| forgotten.
